events.title: Devotional: Elder Neil L. Andersen
events.description:
Elder Neil L. Andersen was named an Apostle of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on April 4, 2009. Elder Andersen was serving as the senior member of the Presidency of the Seventy prior to his calling to the Quorum of the Twelve. He was named a member of the First Quorum of the Seventy in April 1993, at age 41. He previously led the work of the Church in southern Brazil and, again as a member of an area presidency, oversaw the Church in Western Europe. Prior to his call as a General Authority, Elder Andersen served as a mission president in the France Bordeaux Mission and as president of the Tampa Florida Stake.

He graduated from BYU, where he was a Hinckley Scholar, and he earned a Master of Business Administration from Harvard University.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: Ask Me Anything: Inside the Foreign Service Career
events.description:
How can you start preparing for a diplomacy career? What is it really like professionally, for your family, and as a member of the Church?

Ambassador Jeffrey M. Hovenier (ret.) left the State Department in 2024 after more than 34 years in public service representing the US in Europe and Latin America. He developed a record of success as a senior leader and manager of interagency teams to advance US strategic priorities and as a strategist and negotiator. His senior positions included Ambassador to Kosovo and Chargé d’Affaires and Deputy Chief of Mission in Turkey. He also served as Acting Deputy Chief of Mission and Minister Counselor for Political Affairs at the US Embassy to Germany; at embassies in Peru, Greece, Croatia, Paraguay, and Panama; and at the US Mission to the OSCE.

Sponsored by the Kennedy Center for International Studies and the Foreign Service Student Organization.

events.title: Civic Martial Arts: Preparing to Lead in a Polarized America
events.description:
Join us for a lecture from Simon Greer, a nationally recognized bridge builder and social entrepreneur with 30+ years on the front lines of America’s most polarized conflicts. A serial nonprofit founder who has launched seven successful organizations, he leads Cambridge Heath Ventures and co-created Courageous Conversations and Bridging the Gap, initiatives that help students, leaders, and communities navigate division. He has convened dialogues from college campuses to the Middle East to America’s prisons, earning a MidSouth Emmy Award for producing The North Carolina Listening Project. He taught at UNC Chapel Hill as an honorary scholar and is now a Senior Fellow at Harvard’s Kennedy School, where he co-instructs Arguing Israel and Palestine. Greer believes our future depends on our ability to talk to each other across our differences.

Part of the Kennedy Center's fall 2026 lecture series, "Religion, Identity, and Public Life."

Sponsored by the Kennedy Center for International Studies and the Richard L. Evans Chair of Religious Understanding.

events.title: Americans Go to the Moon
events.description:
Join us for "America at the Crossroads," a new series that invites us to think about how movies, music, museums, and more help us understand America’s past and shape our decisions about its future.

In our second installment, hear from Katie Cardon, Deputy Chief System Engineer for the Orion Program at Lockheed Martin.

Artemis II marked America’s return to the Moon after more than fifty years, serving as a powerful symbol of national ambition and collective effort. Hear Cardon, who supported Mission Control at NASA’s Johnson Space Center during the Artemis II mission, talk about how going back to the Moon demonstrated that the greatest achievements come from teamwork and perseverance, uniting people across backgrounds to accomplish something extraordinary. Ultimately, Artemis II reminded Americans of their capacity to work together toward ambitious goals and inspired a renewed sense of shared purpose.

Sponsored by the American Studies program.

events.title: Classic Film: King Kong, 1933

The library has the papers of both the director, Merian C. Cooper, and the score composer, Max Steiner.

Critics called it "thrilling" when was released and it was re-released in various versions over the years before being restored. The library of Congress declared it "culturally, historically and aesthetically significant" and added it to the National Film Registry.

This film is often mentioned when people look at the way 1930's Hollywood portrayed the world.

Admission is free.

events.title: The Role of Faith in Human Flourishing
events.description:
What does it truly mean to flourish—and how can societies help people achieve it?

Drawing on groundbreaking data, Dr. Byron Johnson, Director of the Institute for Global Human Flourishing at Baylor University, will explore the links between faith, well-being, and human flourishing, revealing surprising insights about purpose, relationships, and the pathways to a thriving life. The event will be held at 7pm in the Hinckley Center Assembly Hall at Brigham Young University, serving as the opening keynote address of the Religion and Human Flourishing conference.

This lecture is co-sponsored by Wheatley Institute, Brigham Young University's College of Family, Home, and Social Sciences, and College of Religious Education.

ABOUT THE SPEAKER:

Dr. Byron Johnson is the Director of the Institute for Global Human Flourishing at Baylor University. He is the author of more than 350 journal articles, monographs, and books, focusing much of his professional career on the scientific study of religion, the efficacy of faith-based organizations, and criminal justice. Dr. Johnson is also the project co-director of the Global Flourishing Study. The multi-year data collection and research collaboration has brought researchers from Baylor and Harvard University in partnership with Gallup and the Center for Open Science to gather data from approximately 200,000 participants from 22 countries in order to create an open access resource for researchers, journalists, policymakers, and educators worldwide.

events.title: Deep Roots, Open Arms: Truman G. Madsen Lecture on Eternal Man
events.description:
Must we choose between the security of deep roots — a particular faith, culture, or community that knows its own — and the openness of hospitality toward those who differ from us? Anne Snyder, editor-in-chief of Comment magazine, argues this is a false choice. Drawing on some of America's most generative religious and civic traditions, she explores how our most rooted communities can become schools of hospitality — forming people capable of loving what is distinctly their own while still reaching beyond it.

Her lecture, which represents the 2026 Truman G. Madsen Lecture on Eternal Man, will be held in the Assembly Hall at the Hinckley Center at Brigham Young University.

BYU Professor Truman G. Madsen was a renowned philosopher, teacher, and biographer and is regarded as one of the great thinkers within the Latter-day Saint tradition. One of his goals as a founding senior fellow of Wheatley Institute was to bring academic experts and thought leaders “to the fire” at Brigham Young University. In honor of this goal, the Madsen Lecture brings leading scholars of faith from across the spectrum of religious traditions to BYU and provides them an opportunity to discuss their work on the foundational relationship between faith and reason.

events.title: Devotional: Rebekka Matheson
events.description:
Rebekka Matheson is an associate professor and course director for the Brain, Behavior, and Movement course in the Department of Preparatory Learning at the BYU School of Medicine. She also serves as the chair of the faculty council of the faculty senate for the school of medicine.

On main campus, she serves as the Associate Director of the Neuroscience Center in the College of Life Sciences, and continues to teach classes for the Neuroscience Center every fall. She co-directs the Neuroscience in Europe International Study Program in spring terms. Matheson graduated from the Neuroscience Center at BYU and then went to medical school at the University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry, where her clinical and research work emphasized neurology and addiction medicine. While in Rochester, she completed additional graduate coursework in neuropharmacology and physiology. She currently serves in the Relief Society Presidency for the Utah State Hospital branch.

events.title: Devotional: Bishop L. Todd Budge
events.description:
Bishop L. Todd Budge was named First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric on November 14, 2025. Bishop Budge was sustained as a General Authority Seventy on April 6, 2019, and served in that capacity until his call as Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric in October 2020. Bishop Budge has served in a number of Church callings, including stake president, president of the Japan Tokyo Mission, and Area Seventy.

Bishop Budge received a bachelor of arts degree in economics from BYU in 1984. He worked for Bain & Company Japan; Citibank, N.A.; and GE Capital in both Atlanta and Japan. In 2003 he became president and chief executive officer of Tokyo Star Bank Limited; from 2008 to 2011 he served as chairman of the board. He retired from the bank in 2011. During this time, he also served as a member of the board of directors for Hawaiian Airlines.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

Her lecture will be held at 7:00pm in the Hinckley Center Assembly Hall at Brigham Young University.

Heather Gerken is the 11th president of the Ford Foundation. A nationally recognized expert on democracy, federalism, and elections, Gerken has spent her career working on bipartisan efforts to protect the rule of law.

As president of the Ford Foundation, she leads the $16 billion charitable foundation, which operates offices in the United States and 10 regions around the world.

events.title: Devotional: Elder Ronald A. Rasband
events.description:
Elder Ronald A. Rasband was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on October 3, 2015, after serving as a member of the Presidency of the Seventy since 2005. He has served as a counselor in the Europe Central Area Presidency, president of the Utah Salt Lake City Area, executive director of the Temple Department; and has supervised the North America West, Northwest and three Utah areas as a member of the Presidency of the Seventy.

Elder Rasband attended the University of Utah. In 1987, he was appointed President and Chief Operating Officer of Huntsman Chemical Corporation. When he left Huntsman Chemical Corporation in 1996 to serve as a mission president in New York, he was also serving as a member of the Board of Directors.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: Devotional: Elder Joni L. Koch
events.description:
Elder Joni L. Koch was sustained as a General Authority Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on April 1, 2017. At the time of his call, he had been serving as president of the Mozambique Maputo Mission. He previously served as Second Counselor in the Africa Southeast Area Presidency and President of the Brazil Area. He currently serves in the United States Northeast Area. Elder Koch has served in numerous Church callings, including stake president, Area Seventy and president of the Mozambique Maputo Mission.

Elder Koch received a Bachelor of Science degree in statistics from BYU in 1991. He received an executive MBA from FGV/SP in 1994. During his career he has worked in senior management positions at Cargill Foods, AP Moller Maersk Group, and was the CEO of CM Ltd. at the time of his call as mission president.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

Spend an evening with Jeff Flake, Wheatley Fellow and former U.S. ambassador, as he speaks about democracy, responsibility, and citizenship.

The event will be held at 7:00 PM in the Hinckley Center Assembly Hall.

ABOUT THE SPEAKER:

Jeff Flake, who is originally from Snowflake, Arizona, has served in a wide number of public positions. His experience in politics include 12 years as a House Representative and six years as a Senator for the state of Arizona, and roughly two and a half years as U.S. Ambassador to the Republic of Türkiye. He is also the founding Director of the Institute of Politics at Arizona State University, Chairman of the Board of World Trade Center Utah, and a non-resident fellow of Wheatley Institute.

events.title: The Wonder of Scripture with Alexandra Mackenzie Johns
events.description:
Alexandra Mackenzie Johns will deliver this Wonder of Scripture lecture. She is an assistant professor of Theatre Arts at Brigham Young University, where she focuses on religious theatre, site-specific performance, verbatim theatre, pilgrimage, and practice-as-research. Johns is known for co-leading the Performance, Religion, and Spirituality group within the International Federation for Theatre Research and for presenting internationally on religious theatre.

The Wonder of Scripture series, sponsored by BYU’s Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship, invites speakers from diverse backgrounds to explore how sacred texts shape understanding, inspire wonder, and inform meaningful lives. Each lecture offers a distinctive perspective on scripture and its enduring significance.

events.title: The Hebrew Bible's Ancient Avengers
events.description:
Long before Spider-Man, Wonder Woman, Batman and the Guardians of the Galaxy, the Hebrew Bible’s Ancient Avengers were inspiring Americans. Ripped from the story from ancient Israel, the figures of Samson, Esther, Elijah, and David served as spiritual sustenance to freedom fighters, politicians, and pundits striving to see the United States live up to its founding ideals. In this lecture we will examine how these Hebraic heroes shaped the American story from its founding era to today.

ABOUT THE SPEAKER

Rabbi Dr. Stuart Halpern serves as the senior advisor to the provost as well as the deputy director and chief strategy officer of the Zahava and Moshael J. Straus Center for Torah and Western Thought at Yeshiva University. In addition to his doctorate in education, Rabbi Halpern has master’s degrees in both Bible and Psychology in Education, and an MBA in Nonprofit Management.

events.title: Devotional: Elder Gerrit W. Gong
events.description:
Elder Gerrit W. Gong currently serves as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. He previously served as a member of the Asia Area Presidency and member of the Presidency of the Seventy.

During his 20 years in Washington, D.C., he served as special assistant to the undersecretary of state at the U.S. State Department, as special assistant to the U.S. ambassador in Beijing, China, and in several positions at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, D.C. He was also assistant to the president for planning and assessment at BYU.

Elder Gong holds a doctorate in international relations and a master’s degree in philosophy from Oxford University, where he was a Rhodes scholar. He also holds a bachelor's degree in Asian and university studies from BYU.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.description:
It’s Amsterdam, 1942, and as the Frank family goes into hiding to avoid being deported with other Jews, silence is the rule. Anne’s words stretch beyond the limits of her time, place, and life. This firsthand account of family and friendship in dark times is an anthem to the human spirit.

events.title: Utah Entrepreneur Challenge Application Deadline
events.description:
The Tim Draper Utah Entrepreneur Challenge (UEC) is a statewide, student business competition. Teams from universities across Utah compete for the best student business and a chance to win cash and prizes. We invite all students in Utah from participating colleges and universities to apply. The challenge will culminate with at a final event at the University of Utah. Participating teams are judged by industry professionals, experienced entrepreneurs and community experts. Judges will allocate $75,000 in prizes and awards to the top 20 finalists. Many past winners have developed into successful enterprises. The program is managed by the Lassonde Entrepreneur Institute at the University of Utah. Sponsors include Tim Draper, a renowned venture capitalist.

D. Brett Pennington (BS '94) is a senior energy executive with nearly 30 years of leadership and technical experience in the oil and gas industry. He currently serves as President and Chief Executive Officer of Ensign Natural Resources, a private equity-backed exploration and production company focused on the acquisition, development and optimization of oil and gas assets. The company transformed the asset in just three years before selling to Marathon Oil for approximately $3 billion.

Prior to Ensign, Mr. Pennington held senior executive positions with Murphy Oil Corporation and spent more than a decade with ExxonMobil in engineering, planning, project management, and leadership roles. Mr. Pennington serves on the Board of Directors of the Texas Oil & Gas Association. He holds a bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering from Brigham Young University and completed the Advanced Management Program at Harvard Business School, along with executive programs at Wharton and Thunderbird.

events.title: Applied Analysis Seminar: Ricardo Weder (National Autonomous University of Mexico)
events.description:
Title: Asymptotic stability of Bernstein-Greene-Kruskal (BGK) waves, Landau Damping, and scattering theory

Abstract: We consider the two species (electrons and positive charged ions) Vlasov-Poisson system linearized around BGK waves. We formulate the problem as an equivalent Vlasov-Ampère system, that we write as a
system of Schrödinger type in an appropriate Hilbert space, and with a selfadjoint Vlasov-Ampère operator as a Hamiltonian. We develop a complete stationary scattering theory. We identify the absolutely continuous spectrum and the singular spectrum of the Vlasov-Ampère operator, we construct the generalized Fourier maps, we prove that the wave operators exist, are complete, satisfy Birman’s invariance principle, and that the stationary formulae hold. Using these results we prove that the BGK waves are asymptotically stable. We obtain a precise description of the large time behaviour of the solutions to the Vlasov-Ampère system. Namely, for large times the phase-space densities of electrons and ions are asymptotic to the phase-space densities of solutions of the unperturbed Vlasov-Ampère system. This implies that they follow the trajectories of solutions to Newton’s equations for electrons and ions with the potential of the BGK wave, in the sense that they are transported along these trajectories. Furthermore, we prove that Landau damping holds, that is to say, the electric field tends to zero in pointwise sense for large times.

events.title: Career in Math Talk: Dr. Zach Boyd (UT AI Policy)
Colloquium: Davi Obata (BYU Math)
events.description:
Title: When Deterministic Systems Behave Randomly

Abstract: Chaotic dynamical systems are deterministic, yet their individual trajectories can be extremely difficult to predict. Ergodic theory offers a different point of view: instead of following a single trajectory exactly, we ask whether its long-term statistical behavior can be understood. I will discuss how this perspective allows us to find surprisingly robust patterns inside chaotic dynamics.

Career in Math Talk: Liz Copene
Colloquium: Sebastian Acosta (Baylor College of Medicine)
events.description:
Title: Mathematics of nonlinear ultrasound imaging: Advances and open problems.

Abstract: The Westervelt equation models the propagation of high-intensity ultrasound waves. For medical imaging purposes, it is needed to estimate the parameters in the equation that model wave speed, diffusivity, and nonlinearity. I will discuss up to date progress on this problem, as well as open questions, from the mathematical point of view. I will also present our contribution which shows that by using time-periodic solutions excited from the boundary at a sufficiently high frequency, knowledge of the first- and second-harmonic Cauchy data at the boundary is sufficient to simultaneously determine the wave speed, diffusivity and nonlinearity in the interior of the domain of interest.

events.title: Weekly Seminar - Kevin Roundy
events.description:
Abstract
According to various industry reports, 70-80% of data breaches involve the abuse of privileged accounts. IT administrators face the daunting task of granting the right amount of access to employees and programs that run on major cloud providers and hundreds of applications. There are 68,584 unique permissions just between AWS, GCP, Microsoft Azure, and Salesforce alone, and there is no standardization between systems. In theory, admins can use these permissioning systems to assign just the right amount of access to every employee and program, but for ease of administration they group permissions into roles, each of which contains many permissions. Our measurements indicate that the median user accessed only 8% of the roles assigned to them and used less than 1% of the permissions in a median role in the past 90 days. This means that the typical user has vastly more privilege than required and can cause significant harm if their password is stolen. In this talk we will discuss industry solutions for this problem, and three ways in which Dr. Roundy's research has helped to address this problem: (1) An Al and optimization-driven framework for modeling permission risk, (2) Use of recommendation systems to predict which permissions a user will need in the future based on past usage, (3) An optimization problem designed to simultaneously minimize over-privilege and reduce the number of roles, permissions, and user groups used by the company.
Biography
Dr. Kevin Alejandro Roundy graduated from BYU's Computer Science Department with a bachelor's degree, where he worked in Dr. Michael Goodrich's research lab. For his Ph.D. dissertation from the University of Wisconsin, he built tools to study defensive computer viruses through static and dynamic analysis and studied their obfuscation techniques. He subsequently worked for the Symantec/Norton Research Lab for 11 years, and joined Andromeda Security in 2023 as a Security and Al Researcher. He is a co-author on more than 20 research papers and 100 patents, covering many aspects of computer security. He lives in Los Angeles County and is the father of four daughters, two of whom are BYU students.

He developed a record of success as a senior leader and manager of interagency teams to advance US strategic priorities and as a strategist and negotiator. His senior positions included Ambassador to Kosovo and Chargé d’Affaires and Deputy Chief of Mission in Turkey. events.title: Civic Martial Arts: Preparing to Lead in a Polarized America
events.description:
Join us for a lecture from Simon Greer, a nationally recognized bridge builder and social entrepreneur with 30+ years on the front lines of America’s most polarized conflicts. A serial nonprofit founder who has launched seven successful organizations, he leads Cambridge Heath Ventures and co-created Courageous Conversations and Bridging the Gap, initiatives that help students, leaders, and communities navigate division. He has convened dialogues from college campuses to the Middle East to America’s prisons, earning a MidSouth Emmy Award for producing The North Carolina Listening Project. He taught at UNC Chapel Hill as an honorary scholar and is now a Senior Fellow at Harvard’s Kennedy School, where he co-instructs Arguing Israel and Palestine. Greer believes our future depends on our ability to talk to each other across our differences.
Part of our fall 2026 lecture series, "Religion, Identity, and Public Life."
Sponsored by the Kennedy Center for International Studies and the Richard L. Evans Chair of Religious Understanding.
Event Flyer

events.title: States of America Screening and Discussion Series
events.description:
In honor of the America250 celebration, join us for a weekly screening and discussion about “States of America,” a documentary film series featuring a short film about a resident from each of the 50 US states, made by Professor Brad Barber and BYU Film students.
This week's films will be Idaho and Connecticut and Jane Lopez (Sociology Department) will be the guest speaker. 
Sponsored by the Theatre and Media Arts Department, the American Studies program, BYU OnStage, KQED, and American Public Television.
Event Flyer

events.title: Study Abroad Fair
events.description:
The world is waiting! Learn how you can get out of Provo at the Study Abroad Fair!
Come check out the programs that are available, get your questions answered, and learn how you could further your education while abroad. You can also learn about scholarships and funding opportunities, enjoy shave ice, and enter our airfare giveaway.
This event will be held in the Marigold Quad (the outdoor space just east of the HRCB).
Hope to see you there!
Event Flyer

events.title: Americans Go to the Moon
events.description:
Join us for "America at the Crossroads," a new series that invites us to think about how movies, music, museums, and more help us understand America’s past and shape our decisions about its future.
In our second installment, hear from Katie Cardon, Deputy Chief System Engineer for the Orion Program at Lockheed Martin. 
Artemis II marked America’s return to the Moon after more than fifty years, serving as a powerful symbol of national ambition and collective effort. Hear Cardon, who supported Mission Control at NASA’s Johnson Space Center during the Artemis II mission, talk about how going back to the Moon demonstrated that the greatest achievements come from teamwork and perseverance, uniting people across backgrounds to accomplish something extraordinary. Ultimately, Artemis II reminded Americans of their capacity to work together toward ambitious goals and inspired a renewed sense of shared purpose.
Sponsored by the American Studies program.
Event Flyer

events.title: Mentor Signup
events.description:
Considering a career in global business, law, diplomacy, national security, or development? Then check out this Kennedy Center mentor event, where you can begin the process of designing your career with the help of a Kennedy Mentor! For juniors and seniors.
Event Flyer

events.title: Global Environmental Studies Club Pizza Party
events.description:
Are you a Global Environmental Studies minor, or just curious about the program? Then you're invited to the GES student pizza party! Come eat pizza, learn about GES and meet like-minded students!
Sponsored by the Global Environmental Studies program.
Event Flyer

events.title: Ask Me Anything about Understanding Intelligence Careers
events.description:
Considering a career in national security or intelligence? Learn more and get your questions answered at this Ask Me Anything event with former CIA officer Loren Allen.
Loren Allen spent 25 years working as an Operations Officer or Case Officer within the Directorate of Operations (DO) at the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and spent almost half of his career deployed overseas to locations in South Asia, Southeast Asia and Oceania. He served in leadership positions both in the field and at CIA HQS, managing sensitive intelligence operations in support of US national security. He received a bachelor’s degree in History from BYU History.
Sponsored by the Kennedy Center for International Studies and the National Security Student Association.
Event Flyer

events.title: Boren Scholarship Faculty Info Session
events.description:
Did you know Boren Awards can help your students get $25,000 to study a language overseas for 6 months or longer?
Come to our information session with Michael Saffle, a Boren Awards Program Specialist with the U.S. Department of Defense, to learn about these opportunities available for students interested in foreign languages.
Brazilian esfihas will be served!

events.title: Joy in the Journey: Learn, Grow, Serve
events.description:
The Kennedy Center's 2026 honored alum is Jeremy Andrus. Come hear him deliver his Honored Alumni Lecture at the Kennedy Center, part of Homecoming Week!
Jeremy Andrus (BS '96, MBA ’02) is President and CEO of Traeger Grills, the wood pellet grill brand. He and a financial partner acquired the company in 2014, transforming it from a small, regional, business into a multi-hundred-million-dollar brand that owns over 50% of the global wood pellet grill market.
While Traeger has become Jeremy’s most successful business story, it isn’t his first. He joined the start-up Skullcandy in 2005 with 4 employees and less than $1m in sales. Under his leadership, the headphone company transformed into a $300 million brand. Jeremy was named EY Entrepreneur of the Year in 2016, Mountain West Capital Network Utah Entrepreneur of the Year in 2017, and was inducted into the Utah Technology Council Hall of Fame in 2018. He serves on the board of directors of World Trade Center Utah, GOED, Silicon Slopes, and Utah Olympic Legacy Foundation. Jeremy received his MBA from Harvard Business School and BA from Brigham Young University. He lives in Salt Lake City with his wife Kristin and their six children.
